adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197: Changing existing span-buf:s: Redis keys from sets to sorted sets without migration or versioning causes WRONGTYPE errors for predeployment buffers and prevents mixed-version workers from sharing the keys.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a clear change from Redis SET operations to SORTED SET operations on the same key pattern 'span-buf:s:{project_and_trace}:{parent_span_id}'. In buffer.py line 197, `p.sadd(set_key, ...)` is changed to `p.zadd(set_key, ...)`. In the Lua script (add-buffer.lua), `scard` becomes `zcard`, `sunionstore` becomes `zunionstore`, and `sscan` becomes `zscan`. Redis commands are type-specific - calling ZADD on an existing SET key (or vice versa) will return a WRONGTYPE error. During deployment, if there are existing keys created with the old SET-based code, the new SORTED SET commands will fail. Similarly, if workers running different versions of the code try to operate on the same keys, they will encounter type mismatches. There is no migration strategy, versioning, or key name change to handle this transition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:47: ZUNIONSTORE sums duplicate members' scores by default, inflating timestamps when spans are reprocessed and causing eviction to retain older spans over newer ones; AGGREGATE MAX is needed to preserve timestamp scores.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue. Looking at the Lua script changes, `zunionstore` is used at lines 47 and 52 to merge sorted sets. The code uses `end_timestamp_precise` as scores (seen in buffer.py line 196-198 where `zadd` uses `span.end_timestamp_precise` as the score). When `zunionstore` is called without specifying AGGREGATE, it defaults to SUM behavior for duplicate members. If the same span payload appears in multiple sets being merged, their scores (timestamps) would be summed, resulting in incorrect timestamp values. Later, `zpopmin` is used to evict spans with the lowest scores (oldest timestamps), but if scores are inflated due to summing, the eviction logic would be incorrect - it might retain older spans over newer ones. The fix would be to use `AGGREGATE MAX` to preserve the correct timestamp when duplicates exist.
